```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 7,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(stockplotr)
```

Age and length compositions are often the most informative, and the hardest
to fit, data in a stock assessment. {stockplotr} has a set of plots for
composition data based on the figures that
[r4ss](https://github.com/r4ss/r4ss) makes for Stock Synthesis models. Each
plot shows the data in a different way, and each has an r4ss equivalent:

| Plot | Function | What it shows | r4ss equivalent |
|------|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| Distributions of observations | `plot_comp(show_expected = FALSE)` | The most intuitive way to look at compositions | `SSplotComps()` subplot 1, `datonly = TRUE` |
| Bubble plot of observations | `plot_comp_bubble()` | Cohort strength over time | `SSplotComps()` subplot 2, `datonly = TRUE` |
| Distributions of observed and expected values | `plot_comp()` | An intuitive way to look at fit | `SSplotComps()` subplots 1 and 21 |
| Pearson residuals | `plot_comp_residuals()` | Blocks or stripes of misfit among years or bins | `SSplotComps()` subplots 2 and 24 |
| Sex ratios | `plot_comp_sex_ratio()` | Trends in misfit for bins with small proportions, which have small residuals | `SSplotSexRatio()` |
| Mean age or length (Francis) | `plot_comp_francis()` | Trends among years; Francis (2011) TA1.8 data weights | `SSplotComps()` subplots 8 and 9, `SSMethod.TA1.8()` |
| N-EffN comparison | `plot_comp_sample_size()` | McAllister-Ianelli data weights | `SSplotComps()` subplot 7 |
| Residual distribution | `plot_comp_residual_dist()` | Heavy tails, skewness, and outliers; SDNR | |
| Residual patterns | `plot_comp_residual_pattern()` | Bias by bin or year, with a runs test | |
| Andre's plots | `plot_comp_andre()` | Mean age at length for conditional age-at-length data | `SSplotComps()` subplot 12 |
| Conditional age-at-length residuals | `plot_comp_residuals(conditional = TRUE)` | Misfit by length and age within years | `SSplotComps()` subplot 3 |

Each function can plot fleets separately or summarize all fleets. Use `fleet`
to choose fleets, and `aggregate = TRUE` in `plot_comp()` and
`plot_comp_sex_ratio()` to combine all years.

## Composition data

The plotting functions take composition data in one of several formats and
standardize it with `prepare_comp_data()`:

* A tidy data frame with columns `year`, `bin`, and `observed`, and,
  optionally, `fleet`, `sex`, `part` (partition), `expected`, `n` (sample
  size), `pearson`, and `comp_type` ("age" or "length").
* FIMS output with `observed` and `expected` columns, such as the output of
  `FIMS::get_estimates()`.
* {stockplotr} standard output from `convert_output()` with labels such as
  `age_composition_proportion` and `age_composition_expected`.
* Output from `r4ss::SS_output()`, either the whole list or its `lendbase`,
  `agedbase`, or `condbase` data frames.

This vignette uses data from the 2019 Big Skate stock assessment for the U.S.
West Coast, the same model used for the
[r4ss example plots](https://r4ss.github.io/r4ss/BigSkate/), so the figures
below can be compared directly with the r4ss versions. `bigskate_lencomp`
holds the length compositions (`lendbase` from `r4ss::SS_output()`) and
`bigskate_caal` the conditional age-at-length data (`condbase`), with columns
renamed to follow stockplotr conventions.

```{r}
head(bigskate_lencomp)
```

The length compositions are sex-specific. `Fishery_current` has separate
retained (`part` = 2) and discarded (`part` = 1) compositions, which are
labeled "Fishery_current (retained)" and "Fishery_current (discard)", as in
r4ss. Use `fleet = "Fishery_current"` to select both.

If Pearson residuals are not supplied, `prepare_comp_data()` calculates them
assuming a multinomial distribution,
$r = (o - e) / \sqrt{e (1 - e) / N}$, using the sample size `n`. The Big
Skate data include the residuals reported by Stock Synthesis.

## Observations

Distributions are the most intuitive way to look at compositions. For
sex-specific data, females are shown above zero and males below.

```{r obs-dist, fig.height = 9}
plot_comp(bigskate_lencomp, fleet = "WCGBTS", show_expected = FALSE)
```

Bubble plots make it easier to see patterns across years, such as strong
cohorts moving through the population.

```{r obs-bubble}
plot_comp_bubble(bigskate_lencomp)
```

## Fits to the data

Adding the expected values to the distribution plot shows the fit to each
year. As in r4ss, each panel shows the adjusted input sample size (N adj.)
and the effective sample size (N eff.).

```{r fit-dist, fig.height = 4}
plot_comp(bigskate_lencomp, fleet = "Triennial")
```

Aggregating across years gives an overview of each fleet. Years are weighted
by their adjusted input sample sizes.

```{r fit-agg, fig.height = 6}
plot_comp(bigskate_lencomp, aggregate = TRUE)
```

### Pearson residuals

Pearson residuals are a more statistically rigorous way to look at fit.
Filled bubbles show where more fish were observed than expected, and open
bubbles where fewer were observed. The largest residual in each panel is
included in the label.

```{r resid, fig.height = 8}
plot_comp_residuals(bigskate_lencomp)
```

### Sex ratios

The fraction female in each bin, female / (female + male), can show trends
in misfit for bins with small proportions, since those bins have small
residuals. Vertical lines are Jeffreys intervals based on the sample size in
each bin. For Big Skate, the largest fish are almost all female.

```{r sex-ratio, fig.height = 9}
plot_comp_sex_ratio(bigskate_lencomp, fleet = "WCGBTS")
```

```{r sex-ratio-agg, fig.height = 6}
plot_comp_sex_ratio(bigskate_lencomp, aggregate = TRUE)
```

### Mean length and Francis weights

The time series of mean age or length was developed as a diagnostic for the
Francis (2011) data weighting method (TA1.8), but it is also a useful summary
of trends in the data and the fit. Thick intervals are based on the current
sample sizes, and thin, capped intervals show the result of further adjusting
sample sizes by the TA1.8 weight in each panel label. As in
`r4ss::SSMethod.TA1.8()`, partitions of a fleet are combined into one
composition per year. The weights near one show that this model was already
tuned with the Francis method.

```{r francis, fig.height = 5}
set.seed(1) # the interval for the Francis weight is bootstrapped
plot_comp_francis(bigskate_lencomp)
```

### N-EffN comparison

The effective sample size measures how well the model fits each composition
(McAllister and Ianelli 1997). If the input sample sizes suit the fit, the
points should scatter around the 1:1 line. The ratio of the harmonic mean
effective sample size to the mean input sample size, shown in each panel
label, is the McAllister-Ianelli weight. As in Stock Synthesis, it is
calculated across all partitions of a fleet, and multiplying it by the
current variance adjustment gives the `Recommend_var_adj` that Stock
Synthesis reports.

```{r sample-size, fig.height = 6}
plot_comp_sample_size(bigskate_lencomp)
```

For Stock Synthesis models, the same plot can be made directly from
`convert_output()` output, using the adjusted input and effective sample
sizes that Stock Synthesis reports:

```{r sample-size-ss3}
plot_comp_sample_size(stockplotr::example_data, comp_type = "length")
```

### Residual distribution and patterns

A quantile-quantile plot shows whether residuals have heavier tails than
expected. The standard deviation of the normalized residuals (SDNR) is shown
in each panel label; values well above one suggest the data are given more
weight than the fit supports.

```{r resid-qq, fig.height = 6}
plot_comp_residual_dist(bigskate_lencomp)
```

Averaging residuals by bin or year turns stripes in the bubble plot into a
single line. Filled points fail a runs test, meaning the residual signs in
that bin are not randomly ordered across years.

```{r resid-pattern, fig.height = 8}
plot_comp_residual_pattern(bigskate_lencomp)
```

## Conditional age-at-length data

Conditional age-at-length data are age compositions for each length bin.
Use `conditional = TRUE` in `prepare_comp_data()` and `plot_comp_bubble()`,
and supply a `length_bin` column in tidy data, as in `bigskate_caal`. The Big
Skate conditional data are single-sex compositions, which are normalized
separately for each sex.

`plot_comp_andre()` makes "Andre's plots" from r4ss: the observed and
expected mean age in each length bin (left), and the standard error of the
mean age (right), one row per year and sex.

```{r caal-andre, fig.height = 10}
caal_recent <- dplyr::filter(bigskate_caal, year %in% 2016:2018)
plot_comp_andre(caal_recent, fleet = "WCGBTS")
```

Pearson residuals for conditional data are plotted by length bin and age for
each year:

```{r caal-resid, fig.height = 6}
plot_comp_residuals(caal_recent, fleet = "WCGBTS", conditional = TRUE)
```

## Using model output

With FIMS, pass the estimates directly:

```{r fims, eval = FALSE}
estimates <- FIMS::get_estimates(fit)
plot_comp_residuals(estimates, comp_type = "age")
plot_comp_francis(estimates, comp_type = "length")
```

FIMS reports years as indices (`year_i`); add a `year` column to plot
calendar years. FIMS estimates do not currently include composition sample
sizes. Add an `n` column, or supply Pearson residuals in a `pearson` column,
to get residuals and intervals.

With Stock Synthesis, use the output of `r4ss::SS_output()`. Pearson residuals
and adjusted sample sizes are taken from the model output, the Francis
weights match `r4ss::SSMethod.TA1.8()`, and the effective sample sizes and
McAllister-Ianelli weights match those reported by Stock Synthesis.
Conditional age-at-length data come from the `condbase` element:

```{r ss3, eval = FALSE}
replist <- r4ss::SS_output("path/to/BigSkate_2019")
plot_comp(replist, comp_type = "length", fleet = "WCGBTS")
plot_comp_francis(replist, comp_type = "length")
plot_comp_andre(replist, fleet = "WCGBTS")
```

## References

Francis, R.I.C.C. (2011). Data weighting in statistical fisheries stock
assessment models. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 68:
1124-1138.

McAllister, M.K., and Ianelli, J.N. (1997). Bayesian stock assessment using
catch-age data and the sampling-importance resampling algorithm. Canadian
Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 54: 284-300.

Taylor, I.G., Gertseva, V., Stephens, A., and Bizzarro, J. (2019). Status of
Big Skate (*Beringraja binoculata*) off the U.S. Pacific Coast in 2019.
Pacific Fishery Management Council, Portland, OR.
